Finca Las Margaritas is based on extensive volcanic wasteland that since 3 or 4 million years ago covered the coastal platform of Las Galletas. In this large agricultural area of 825 Ha is located the largest bananas plantations in greenhouse of Tenerife, where moves a volume of more than 26 thousand tons for export anually. FINCA LAS MARGARITAS began with the cultivation of banana in Las Galletas in the year 1977, the union and several family members of Adolfo Guerra González entrepreneurship and Margarita Hernández Pérez, later named the estate, being 86 years old in 2012. Both came from a long family generation of farmers in S/C de La Palma and San Andrés y Sauces. On this farm are produces 2 cultivars of Canary Island banana, the great dwarf and the thick Palm or small dwarf, the Dwarf Cavendish variety, reaching an average of 45-50 klg per bunch, and can find copies that they exceed the 70 klg. The acreage is of approximately 7 Ha with 98% of bananas and 2% of fruit trees such as: mango, papaya and avocado.

The Ethnographic Park and Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar is a large open-air museum and one of the five official botanical gardens of the Canary Islands. The Park was founded in 1998 by the renowned Norwegian researcher Thor Heyerdahl, who was responsible for safeguarding the pyramids from an urban development plan. In addition to the pyramids, the Park includes four outdoor trails and specialised gardens, spread over more than 64,000m2. The routes allow visitors to stroll freely through the extensive gardens, discovering interesting aspects of Canarian culture and nature. These routes include a Canarian Botanical Route, a Cultural Route and a Volcanic Route. The facilities also include the Casa Chacona Museum and an Auditorium. As for its botanical collections, you can visit the Poison Garden, unique in Spain, and the Sustainable Garden, a reproduction of a Canarian ravine, including a watercourse and presenting the flora characteristic of these environments in a sustainable way. The Tropicarium shows the life strategies used by orchids and insectivorous plants to survive in tropical conditions. The Park was the winner of the 'Best Overall Sustainable Tourism Practice 2021' award for the island of Tenerife and a national finalist in the 'Remarkable Venue Awards 2022' in the Best Hidden Gem category, which highlights the most outstanding and special places for travellers from all over the world. The Park has also been awarded the Biosphere Committed distinction for its sustainable commitment and is a member of the Climate Heritage Network. The Ethnographic Park and Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar offers a unique outdoor experience, without crowds of people thanks to its 30,000m2 of accessible garden areas, allowing culture and nature lovers to enjoy a day outdoors in a different, safe and sustainable environment.

The Pascua Florida festival in Guía de Isora is one of the most emblematic cultural events of Holy Week in southern Tenerife . These works reinterpret the Passion of Christ through ephemeral compositions that combine color, symbolism, and design. The Easter Flower Festival in Guía de Isora is a benchmark for cultural tourism in Tenerife . Each floral arrangement is unique and unrepeatable , making this event one of the most singular cultural experiences on the island during Holy Week. Visiting the Easter celebrations in Guía de Isora means discovering a tradition that blends art, spirituality, and historical heritage in the heart of southern Tenerife. It's an event that surprises, moves, and attracts visitors each year who seek to experience Holy Week in Tenerife from an artistic and unique perspective.

Finally, we will resume our hike and continue admiring everything this incredible natural space has to offer on the way back.

Our first visit will be to the Teide National Park, located in the heart of Tenerife and home to the highest peak in Spain: the volcano El Teide. Here we will stop for about 30 minutes to admire the impressive volcanic landscapes of Las Cañadas del Teide, not forgetting the emblematic Roques de García. After this visit, we will descend to Icod de los Vinos where we will have the opportunity to contemplate the famous Drago Milenario, which is said to be more than 800 years old. You will have free time to have lunch on your own or enjoy the Canarian gastronomy tasting one of the menus that we recommend in some of the restaurants in the area. The next destination is Garachico, a colourful coastal village with a history marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. Here we will stroll through the streets of its historic quarter, recognised as a Cultural Heritage Site and one of the most representative of the Canary Islands, and discover emblematic sites such as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by lava flows, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that defended the town from pirate attacks. We will follow the route and enter the vibrant nature of the Teno Rural Park until we reach the hamlet of Masca, located between impressive valleys and ravines. Let yourself be surprised by the charm of the traditional architecture of this enclave, declared a Site of Ethnographic and Historical Interest and an Asset of Cultural Interest.

Flavors and Wines of Tenerife: A Journey for the Senses On this excursion through southern Tenerife, you will discover the island's most authentic flavors and renowned wines, with the convenience of returning to your accommodation in time to continue enjoying your day. We will start with a visit to Finca Las Margaritas, where you will learn about traditional banana cultivation and taste products made with gofio, palm honey, and tropical fruits. Then, we will enjoy the breathtaking views along the mountain road to Vilaflor, until we reach Bodega Lagar de Chasna, where we will have a wine tasting paired with a delicious selection of the best Canarian gastronomy. After this experience, we will return so you can make the most of the rest of your day.

Would you like to discover the island of La Gomera on a single day trip from Tenerife? Then this is your perfect option! Our day starts by heading to the port of Los Cristianos, where we will take a ferry to the island. Once here, we'll board the bus and head into the Hermigua Valley, where we'll have the opportunity to capture some photos of the breathtaking scenery. We will continue the excursion until we reach the municipality of Agulo, where we will enjoy a delicious lunch in a typical restaurant with local products. If availability permits, during lunch we will witness a live demonstration of "silbo gomero", a unique language declared Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. After lunch we will enter the Garajonay National Park, a paradise of laurel forests and a nature reserve also declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Laguna Grande we will learn all the curiosities of this magical place where it is said that the witches of the island used to meet. We will make a stop at the imposing Roque de Agando, one of the most emblematic places of La Gomera. Finally, we will arrive in San Sebastián, the capital of the island. Here we will have the opportunity to discover the last traces left by Christopher Columbus after his passage through La Gomera, such as the Torre del Conde or the Casa Colón. Once we have finished our visit of San Sebastian, we will head back to the ferry to Tenerife.

This excursion gives you the opportunity to get to know the essence of Tenerife in just one day. We will start the day by visiting Candelaria. This coastal town is home to the Basilica of Candelaria, one of the most important places of worship in Tenerife. On the seashore you can admire the imposing bronze statues commemorating the ancient Guanche Kings of Tenerife. The excursion continues in the Historic-Artistic Site of La Villa de La Orotava. The cobbled streets of its historic quarter will take us to places full of charm and culture such as La Casa de Los Balcones, the Town Hall Square or the Church of Nuestra Señora de La Concepción. We will continue our journey through the north of Tenerife until we reach Garachico, a charming coastal town, whose history is marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. We will stroll through its historic centre, declared a Site of Cultural Interest, and visit such emblematic places as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by volcanic lava, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that protected the town from pirate attacks. Here you will have free time to have lunch on your own or taste the Canarian gastronomy in one of the restaurants we recommend. After this visit, we will enter the Teno Rural Park where we will enjoy its impressive natural landscapes. Its winding roads will take us to Masca, a hamlet surrounded by spectacular cliffs that preserves its traditional Canarian architecture.

This excursion perfectly blends history, culture, and nature. Discover Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Anaga, and San Cristóbal de La Laguna: three must-see gems in the north of Tenerife. Our first stop will be in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, the capital of the island. We will stroll through its vibrant streets, leading us to its most iconic spots, such as Plaza de España, Plaza Weyler, or the Mercado de Nuestra Señora de África. Next, we will venture into the Anaga massif, an impressive natural area declared a Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, you can enjoy some of its most representative viewpoints, like the Mirador de la Jardina or the Mirador Cruz del Carmen, offering spectacular views of the island. Finally, we will continue to San Cristóbal de La Laguna, the first city founded in Tenerife after its conquest and a historic gem declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1999. We will walk through its historic and culturally rich streets, discovering its most significant monuments, such as the Cathedral of San Cristóbal de La Laguna or Plaza del Adelantado. You will have time to enjoy lunch and taste the delicious Canarian cuisine in one of the charming restaurants in the city. After a day of discovering several of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points. We will continue our journey into the Anaga mountain range, a stunning natural area declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, we will visit some of its most iconic viewpoints, such as the Mirador de la Jardina and the Mirador Cruz del Carmen. After a day exploring some of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points.

On this excursion you will have the opportunity to enjoy a relaxing day, stroll around and choose what to see, do and where to sunbathe and swim. We will start our day by going to the south of Tenerife, specifically to Los Cristianos, a place that maintains its seafaring charm. It is the centre of commercial and cultural activity in the region, and numerous maritime connections depart from its port. In addition, every Tuesday and Sunday, there is a street market with a wide variety of products. You will have the whole day free to enjoy this area at your leisure. If your aim is to enjoy a wonderful day at the beach, you will have both Playa de Las Vistas and Playa de Los Cristianos at your disposal. Take the opportunity to go for a dip, or stroll around the shopping area. In the afternoon, we will meet in Los Cristianos to head to the north of the island and return to the pick-up points.

Discover with us the charming town of Puerto de la Cruz, located in the coastal area of the Orotava Valley, in the north of Tenerife. You will have the whole day at your leisure to enjoy a pleasant day by the sea and discover all that this town has to offer. Despite its popularity with travellers who visit the island every year, Puerto de la Cruz has not lost its seaside charm. You can stroll through its beautiful streets and squares, such as the Plaza del Charco or the Muelle Viejo. Many people believe that one of the most outstanding attractions of the municipality is its mild climate that is maintained throughout the year, a fact that was described by several European naturalists who visited Puerto de la Cruz in the 18th and 19th centuries. You will have the opportunity to walk around the city and discover such emblematic places as the Botanical Gardens or the spectacular Martiánez Lake, and end the day watching the waves break on the coast of San Telmo.

Embark on an unforgettable adventure and dive into the essence of La Gomera, the hidden gem of the Canary Islands. In a small group of maximum 18 people, you'll explore spectacular landscapes, ancient forests, and picturesque villages that preserve the island's most authentic character. From San Sebastián de La Gomera, a town full of history and charm, to the stunning viewpoints of Roque de Agando and Valle Gran Rey, every corner of the island will amaze you with its natural beauty. Enter the Garajonay National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the laurel forest wraps the landscape in a magical and mysterious atmosphere. You'll visit Chipude and El Cercado, known for their pottery tradition, and have the chance to discover the Silbo Gomero, a unique whistled language recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. During the tour, you'll enjoy the peaceful charm of small towns like Igualero, the highest village on the island, and immerse yourself in the history and culture of this Canarian jewel. You'll also have the option to taste the island's delicious cuisine, with typical products such as almogrote, gofio, and palm honey. This excursion includes everything you need for a carefree experience: an official Canary Islands guide, ferry tickets, and comfortable transport in an air-conditioned bus. Just relax and let yourself be swept away by the magic of La Gomera. Don't miss the chance to discover this fascinating island in an exclusive and personal way. Book now and get ready for a journey you'll never forget.

Discover the Teide National Park, the most visited in Europe, on this guided tour that includes tickets for the cable car ride up and down. Explore the impressive volcanic landscapes of Las Cañadas del Teide accompanied by an official guide, while you learn about its history and geological formation. Teide, at 3,718 metres, is the highest peak in Spain and the third highest volcano on the planet measured from the seabed. Its geological history goes back hundreds of thousands of years, with successive eruptions that have shaped the landscape of Las Cañadas del Teide, where you will find lava flows from different eras and spectacular rock formations. From the top cable car station, you can choose between three viewpoints and trails to admire the landscape: La Rambleta viewpoint - Panoramic views of Siete Cañadas and the Ucanca Valley. Sendero de La Fortaleza - Perfect for contemplating the north of Tenerife with its forests and cliffs. Pico Viejo Viewpoint Trail - Breathtaking views of the 800 metre diameter crater of Pico Viejo and the neighbouring islands. With your booking, you will have free access to the Teide Legend digital audio guide, available in 8 languages (Spanish, English, German, French, Italian, Russian, Polish and Dutch). This audio guide will allow you to discover the history, geology and biodiversity of the National Park, as well as to learn in detail about the three trails that start from the top station of the cable car. The excursion also includes access to the Science and Legend exhibition, located in the Teide Cable Car Visitor Centre. Through this exhibition, you will learn about the last great eruption of Teide, which occurred approximately 1,000 years ago, and how the ancient Guanches interpreted this natural phenomenon as a battle between their gods. With the audio guide, you can explore this exhibition in the language of your choice. This collective transport tour is the best way to explore Teide in a responsible way, reducing the environmental impact and helping to conserve this World Heritage Site. Book now and live the experience of being at the top of Tenerife!

We will travel by ferry from Tenerife to Gran Canaria in the most comfortable and fastest way with Fred Olsen Express. Arriving at Puerto de las Nieves in Agaete, we will head straight to the historic quarter of Vegueta, where we will take a walking tour through its streets full of culture and history. After exploring Vegueta, we'll head to the Poema del Mar aquarium in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. This impressive theme park, which opened on 17 December 2017, will immerse us in the majesty of nature in three incomparable environments: jungle, beach reef and deep ocean. The 12,000-square-metre facility features 35 marine and river ecosystems from around the globe. The aquarium pays tribute, with its name and architectural lines, to the Canarian artist Néstor de la Torre, who stood out in the avant-garde of the early 20th century, and his work "Poemas del Atlántico" (Poems of the Atlantic). Here we can admire the largest curved glass in the world (a methacrylate weighing 140 tons, 36 metres long and 7 metres high), which exhibits some 350 species from 35 different ecosystems, from sharks, piranhas, freshwater rays, crocodiles and sea dragons. Our last stop will be the Arehucas distilleries, where we will learn the secret of the uniqueness of its rums, a journey through the history, tradition and know-how of Arehucas. During the visit we will explore one of the oldest rum cellars in Europe, made up of 4,308 American oak casks, some even signed by famous personalities. Here we will be explained the process of elaboration of this drink, and we will enjoy a tasting of rums and liqueurs to end the day with a good taste in our mouths. After this experience, we will return to Puerto de las Nieves in Agaete to take the ferry back to Tenerife.

Experiencing the island of La Palma to the fullest is possible with this day trip from Tenerife, perfect for those who wish to discover the landscapes, history, and volcanic impact of this gem in the Canary archipelago. The activity begins upon arrival in Santa Cruz de La Palma, where a guided tour takes visitors through its charming historic center, considered one of the most beautiful and best-preserved in the Canaries. During the walk, participants visit the local market La Recova and admire the famous colonial-style balconies that define the city's traditional architecture. The itinerary continues with a stop at the Mirador de La Cumbrecita, located in the Caldera de Taburiente National Park, a stunning natural setting with unique views of La Palma's mountainous heart. Next, the tour heads to the ground zero of the Tajogaite volcano, following the newly built road across the solidified lava flows. From here, travelers witness striking views of Todoque and the homes destroyed by the eruption—a powerful and moving experience that reflects the magnitude of nature's force. Free time is included, allowing each traveler to explore at their own pace, shop, or enjoy local cuisine at one of the nearby restaurants. Meals are not included, offering more flexibility and making the most of the time on the island. An ideal choice for those seeking a day excursion from Tenerife to La Palma, combining history, natural beauty, and recent volcanic activity in one unforgettable experience.

Enjoy a complete excursion around the island of La Palma, also known as the Beautiful Island. In the afternoon, the group will head to the Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Snows, a pilgrimage site dedicated to the island's patron saint. From this elevated spot, you can enjoy magnificent views of the mountainous landscape and the valley. The tour ends with the return to the Santa Cruz de La Palma dock, with enough time to board and continue your journey.

This is a perfect excursion for astronomy lovers. You will start the tour at the Teide Observatory, where you will do a guided tour. There, your Starlight guide (specialist in the observation of the night sky) will explain the importance of the Canary sky, the telescopes of the observatory and the different projects of the Astrophysics Institute of the Canary Islands. You will also enjoy the sun as never before, since you can observe its spots and flares through the telescope. You will see the sunset from the Observatory, a unique spectacle in which the sun hides behind El Teide. A range of colors will adorn the views of the volcano and the ocean. Then we will go to the base of the Teide's Cable Car and, far from the light pollution of urban areas, you will discover the secrets of the sky in an astronomical observation with the naked eye and with a long-range telescope. Did you know that from El Teide you can see 83 of the 88 constellations officially recognized? You will discover stars, planets, galaxies and clusters as you have never imagined, while your Starlight guide teaches you the constellations, the celestial map and provides you with interesting information about the objects you observe. Marvel at the immensity of the universe and live an experience without equal, in one of the most visited national parks in the world. It also includes a stop for a meal. You choose whether you prefer to bring your own food, use the Cable Car's vending machines or buy the optional picnic along with your ‘Astronomic Tour including a visit of Teide Observatory'.

Discover the Teide National Park like never before: under the starry blanket of night. This nocturnal excursion will take you to explore the beauty of Teide at dusk, when the landscape is transformed and the sky reveals 83 of the 88 known constellations. During the ascent, you will cross different ecosystems, from rural areas and forests to high mountain scrubland, home to native plants such as broom and summit rosebush. You will also see small bats, harmless companions of the night, which live in the volcanic tunnels of the park. These tunnels are also home to unique creatures adapted to total darkness, many of them exclusive to this environment. Teide's sky is one of the best on the planet for stargazing. The scarce light pollution of the environment gives you a clear, sharp sky dome full of mythological stories and mysteries, which you can discover in full with the help of the Starlight guides, who will be at your disposal throughout the observation. This will take place at the cable car base station, at an altitude of 2,356 metres, with professional long-range telescopes. Among volcanoes, with the colours of a natural treasure such as this wild enclave and with the nerves of being about to discover planets, galaxies, clusters and -if there is a full moon- a whole lunar geography that will make you dream. A unique experience that combines the magic of nature and astronomy in a spectacular setting.

Night Skies Tenerife offers a variety of ways to explore our Universe, from the Teide National Park. Be amazed by the majesty of the night sky, through lasers, high-powered telescopes and the humour of their expert astronomy guides. The tours are adapted to all audiences: from children to adults, astronomy lovers or tourists looking for a different and special tour. Enjoy an enchanting sunset and watch the stars shine like nowhere else. Feel the thrill of watching the breathtaking sunset from the highest peak in Spain. The Teide cable car will take you to an altitude of 3,555m to enjoy the spectacle of Teide's shadow on the horizon. After sunset, you can enjoy a picnic dinner at the Cable Car Base Station. The sky of the Teide National Park is one of the best on the planet for stargazing. After dinner, located in the car park at the base station of the cable car, our Starlight guides will show you the fascinating world of the night sky with the help of their long-range telescopes.

The original Teide by Night! A Stargazing experience, spectacular sunsets, a truly enjoyable, informative and unique experience not to be missed We commence the afternoon by driving up through the pine forests to the National Park, taking in the panoramic views of Mount Teide and making stops at the most emblematic points ideal for camera lovers. At approximately 2000m above sea level, you will be stunned as you look out over the Atlantic Ocean across the blanket of clouds to the neighbouring Island of La Gomera and witness one of the most beautiful sunsets. In Las Cañadas del Teide we will stop at one of the highest restaurants on Tenerife, here you will be served a delicious three course mea accompanied by Spanish wines Mount Teide National Park is the ideal location for stargazing activities with the skies and atmospheric conditions being amongst the best in the world for astronomical observation. Crowne d a "Starlight Destination" recognising that it is one of the best places to stargaze away from light pollution your eyes will be in for a treat as you will be guided by our professional, starlight certified guides on a tour of the galaxy. Using laser technology and telescopes you will receive a full explanation of all the night skies have to offer. A truly breathtaking, memorable experience.

If you are an astronomy lover or are looking for a unique experience, a visit to Teide in Tenerife is a must. The island is known for its stunning natural beauty and clear skies, making it an ideal place for stargazing. At 3,718 metres high, Mount Teide is the highest point in Spain and offers spectacular views of the night sky. The Teide National Park tour offers the opportunity to enjoy a spectacular sunset and an unforgettable astronomical experience. Departures are from various points in Costa Adeje, Playa de las Americas and Los Cristianos. Along the way, you can admire the breathtaking landscapes of the island and witness a sunset that paints the sky with an incredible variety of colours. The route continues up to an altitude of 2,000 metres, where the real magic begins. The Teide National Park, free of light pollution and certified as a Starlight destination, allows you to enjoy clear, crisp views of the starry sky, offering the opportunity to observe shooting stars like never before. To enhance the experience, powerful lasers are used to point out constellations, important stars and astronomical navigation techniques. With the use of powerful telescopes, you can observe the surface of the moon (when visible), planets, nebulae, star clusters and, under optimal conditions, the Andromeda galaxy. During certain times of the year, the Milky Way can also be photographed using a mobile phone through the telescope. At the end of the tour, you will return to your starting point, taking with you unforgettable memories of this unique experience.

Are you looking for a different, fun, and adrenaline-filled experience during your stay in Tenerife? In Tenerife, from the highest volcano to the Seaside, on a Bike and without pedaling.The joy of the downhill biking and the beauty of the real hidden Tenerife. 22 miles touring down surfaced roads, without pedaling, in a group with a Guide and a support vehicle, at a very relaxed speed and stopping briefly to take pictures, have a drink or sample the local tapas Since 1999, we've shown you the real Tenerife and we do it the nicest way: on a bicycle!. From the National Park of Mount Teide to the seaside, crossing volcanoes, forests, villages and wastelands, with beautiful views, and all of it downhill. Come with us to spend the most special day of your holidays, call us and well take care of everything from picking you up to dropping you off.When booking we will agree to a pick up point that is convenient for you and a certain time when we will collect you, generally just outside your Hotel or Apt. with a minibus. We will then drive up to the starting point, which is very close to the base of Mount Teide, and if you have not yet seen the National Park, we will drive a little bit further ( its only a couple miles away) so that you do not miss it! Driving up to the starting point, which is 7,200 fl high, will take aprox. one and a half hours. Once at the starting point, we will give you some printed instructions, in your language, about safety rules and the signals we will use during the trip. We will also fit you with helmet, gloves and a high visibility vest, complemented, in winter, with windbreaker jacket and / or leggings. Also with a bicycle your size, of course!.If you carry bags, rucksacks, bottles or other objects, you can, if you wish, for your comfort leave them in the support vehicle, which is always just behind the group. We will travel at a moderate speed, keeping our group together, and we will make several stops ( every 3 miles or so) to take photos, have a drink ( hot or cold, depending on the season) or enjoy a picnic with cheese, olives, bread, water or wine in winter or, in summer, sangria and fresh fruits of the season. ALL included in the price.While we are riding our bikes we will cross volcanic landscapes, thick pine forests, small villages where grapes and potatoes are still grown, other, almost desertic areas, and sll sorts of roads, always surfaced, till our arrival to the seaside, after some 20 or 22 miles, depending on the day. The trip down takes approximately two and a half hours. Once arrived, we will celebrate the completion of the trip with a toast of Spanish Cava and then we will drive you back to your Hotel.

For the Guanches, the aboriginal Canary Islanders, Mount Teide was a volcano considered sacred since ancient times, like Mount Fuji, Mount Olympus or Mount Kilimanjaro. This visit to Pico del Teide by cable car allows you to contemplate the landscape of the largest National Park in the Canary Islands from a height of 3555 metres above sea level. Its particular climate, altitude and volcanic forms invite you to contemplate and enjoy a unique moment that you will remember for the rest of your life. A visit to the Teide volcano is always different, the effects of the light throughout the day and the seasons with their climatic changes give the landscape an ever new appearance. However, two sensations remain constant: the immensity of the landscape and the magnificent silence. The Teide Volcano is at its most emblematic at sunrise and sunset. The spectacular nature of these moments is marked by the different tones of the sky and the light reflected on the rocks. If you want to go up to the Teide cable car you must select "Cable car for excursion" in our excursion Teide National Park.

Make your dream of enjoying the Universe professionally and from one of the best places in the world to see the stars come true: El Teide. The astronomical instrumentation you will have at your disposal during this astronomical observation in Tenerife, together with the quality and transparency of the Tenerife sky from the Teide National Park, far from the light pollution of the big cities, will surely make you enjoy a unique experience in which it will seem as if the stars of Tenerife are almost at your side.

The Canary Islands is one of the three best spots in the world to observe the sky, along with Chile and Hawaii. The Museum of Illusions contains a permanent exhibition is a 700 m2 space filled with illusions, scientific inventions and artistic expressions where physics and optics share space with mysterious works of art and classic riddles. Do you have questions about how an invention works, do you want to hear amazing stories about art and history, do you want to expand your scientific knowledge or capture the moment with a photo? The museum team is always there for you! Its assistants are ready to reveal the secrets of the incredible world of illusions with a smile on their faces. The permanent exhibition often undergoes small changes and new items are added to the collection every year. The museum team is constantly researching and exploring the world of science and art in search of new artistic solutions.

Embark on this comfortable four-wheel adventure and feel what it's like to be part of the north.

Discover the luxury of visiting such a wonderful island as La Gomera aboard one of Tamarán's spacious minivans, designed to make your VIP Tour to La Gomera unforgettable. Let the team tell you everything about what you visit and immerse yourself fully in an island that was the prelude to the discovery of America by Christopher Columbus. This tour takes you from your accommodation — or a nearby point — to the places that make this island so special, which proudly has its own language, the Gomero Whistle (Silbo Gomero), declared World Heritage. This excursion includes a stop at a typical restaurant where you'll savor some of the most characteristic dishes of the islands' gastronomy.

If what you want is to exclusively enjoy the Teide National Park in a big way and only with your friends, without anyone else, discovering all the corners of one of the most visited National Parks in the world, Teide VIP Tour is the excursion you and your friends are looking for. On this Teide tour, you'll enjoy 8 hours of truly spectacular volcanic landscapes. You'll also discover the volcanoes that caused the most recent eruptions in Tenerife and learn about the history of how the Canary Islands were formed. Surely after this group tour, you and your friends can play a mini-Teide trivia game! The Teide Tour does not include lunch, although your group will have free time to eat calmly and talk about how much fun you're having!

Enjoy exclusive access to witness the transformation of Teide National Park at sunset and be amazed by the starry sky, one of the purest on the planet. In this VIP experience, you will explore the different ecosystems of the Park on a private and comfortable ascent, from rural landscapes and laurel forests to the high mountain, home to unique species such as broom and rosalillo de cumbre. Along the way, you will discover little-known natural secrets, such as volcanic tunnels that host creatures adapted to darkness and discreet native bats flying through the night. As night falls, the sky of Teide becomes an unrivalled stage: under a crystal-clear atmosphere, free from light pollution, you will have the chance to admire 83 of the 88 known constellations, planets, clusters, and distant galaxies. All accompanied by your private Starlight guide, who will reveal myths, curiosities, and mysteries of the cosmos, while you enjoy personalised attention. The observation will take place in a unique location, the base station of the cable car, at 2,356 metres above sea level, with professional long-range telescopes at your disposal. On full moon nights, you will discover in detail the fascinating lunar geography, as if walking on its surface. An exclusive, intimate, and sophisticated journey that combines the best of nature, astronomy, and the pleasure of travelling in style.

This excursion is designed for true astronomy enthusiasts who wish to enjoy personalized attention, without rush, and in an intimate atmosphere. You will begin the experience at the Teide Observatory, with a private guided visit in the afternoon. Your Starlight guide, an expert in night-sky observation, will explain in a close and engaging way the importance of the Canary skies, how the telescopes work, and the most outstanding projects of the Canary Islands Astrophysics Institute. You will also observe the sun as never before, discovering sunspots and flares through a specialized telescope. Afterwards, you will enjoy a unique sunset from the Observatory itself, where the sun hides behind majestic Mount Teide and the sky is painted with colors illuminating the volcano and the ocean. At nightfall, we will move to the base of the Teide Cable Car, far from any light pollution. There you will take part in an exclusive astronomical observation, both with the naked eye and through long-range telescopes. From this privileged spot, 83 of the 88 officially recognized constellations can be observed. You will discover stars, planets, galaxies, and clusters as never before, while your guide teaches you to interpret the celestial map and shares with you fascinating facts about the universe. An unrepeatable experience in one of the most spectacular national parks on the planet.

Your guided climb to Teide summit with your own private guide begins at Montaña Blanca at 2,320 m. What can you expect from this route to the Teide crater? You'll begin the route on paths of pumice stone and lava; a low gradient ascending walk that lasts an hour and a half. The path narrows and a there's a slight incline before you reach the Altavista Refuge at 3,260 m. There you will take a rest to eat and let your bodies adapt to the pressure and climate. You will continue on paths of solidified lava until you reach the Teide Cable Car station (3,550 m). You will behold some spectacular views of the Teide National Park and the island of Tenerife from the cable car upper station. ​ The climax of your epic ascent on foot to the peak of Teide with your own private guide is the final stretch to the Teide crater. The ascent will be much harder but the reward will be worth it. After the final effort you'll enjoy time to relax and take in the magnificent panoramic views of the Canary Archipelago from an altitude of 3,718 m.

Can you imagine exploring Tenerife with a totally personalised tour accompanied by an expert guide?
